text: grep -n "fn is_superglobal" -A25 src/superglobals.rs: / script MENTIONS IT BY NAME; a string subscript of `$GLOBALS` is not a mention. Probing 67-/// with `isset($_ENV)` answers true, and the set is SEVEN: 68-/// 69-/// ```text 70-/// php -n -r 'var_dump(isset($_ENV), isset($_REQUEST), isset($_SESSION));' 71-/// bool(true) bool(true) bool(false) 72-/// ``` 73-/// 74-/// Only `$_SESSION` is genuinely absent until `session_start()`. 75-/// 76-/// The distinction is observable and both halves are pinned by tests: a CLI 77-/// `count($_SERVER)` must answer a number rather than raise `count(): Argument #1 78-/// ($value) must be of type Countable|array, null given`, while `isset($_SESSION)` 79-/// must stay false.
